question.de: Muss meine Software, die Laborwerte nur anzeigt, nach MDR als Medizinprodukt eingestuft werden?
question.en: Does my software that only displays laboratory values have to be qualified as a medical device under the MDR?

de.text: Die Quellen beantworten die Frage nur teilweise. Nach Erwägungsgrund 19 ist Software in eigenem Recht ein Medizinprodukt, wenn der Hersteller sie speziell für einen medizinischen Zweck bestimmt. Software für allgemeine Zwecke, auch im Gesundheitswesen, ist keines [1]. Ob Ihre Software, die Laborwerte nur anzeigt, eine solche medizinische Zweckbestimmung hat, geht aus den Quellen nicht hervor. Falls sie als Medizinprodukt gilt, ordnet Anhang VIII Nr. 6.3 Software, die Informationen liefert, die für diagnostische oder therapeutische Entscheidungen genutzt werden, der Klasse IIa zu, bei möglichen schwerwiegenderen Auswirkungen der Klasse IIb oder III [2]. Alle übrige Software ist Klasse I [2]. Die Quellen beschreiben nicht, ob eine reine Anzeige unter diese Entscheidungsregel fällt, und enthalten keine Definition des Medizinprodukts. Eine rechtliche Bewertung kann ich nicht geben.

sources.title: Recital 19
sources.citation: MDR Recital 19 [recital of the original 2017 text]
sources.quote: It is necessary to clarify that software in its own right, when specifically intended by the manufacturer to be used for one or more of the medical purposes set out in the definition of a medical device, qualifies as a medical device, while software for general purposes, even when used in a healthcare setting, or software intended for life-style and well-being purposes is not a medical device. The qualification of software, either as a device or an accessory, is independent of the software's location or the type of interconnection between the software and a device.

sources.title: Annex VIII: CLASSIFICATION RULES > CHAPTER III - CLASSIFICATION RULES > 6. ACTIVE DEVICES > 6.3. Rule 11
sources.quote:
Software intended to provide information which is used to take decisions with diagnosis or therapeutic purposes is classified as class IIa, except if such decisions have an impact that may cause:
— death or an irreversible deterioration of a person's state of health, in which case it is in class III; or
— a serious deterioration of a person's state of health or a surgical intervention, in which case it is classified as class IIb.
Software intended to monitor physiological processes is classified as class IIa, except if it is intended for monitoring of vital physiological parameters, where the nature of variations of those parameters is such that it could result in immediate danger to the patient, in which case it is classified as class IIb.
All other software is classified as class I.

en.text: The passages do not settle this directly, but they set the test. Software is a medical device only if the manufacturer specifically intends it for one or more of the medical purposes in the definition [1][2]. Software for general purposes, even in a healthcare setting, is not a medical device [2]. The listed purposes include "providing information by means of in vitro examination of specimens derived from the human body" [1]. The passages do not say whether software that only displays laboratory values, without diagnostic or other medical purpose stated by the manufacturer, falls within that purpose. Whether it does depends on the intended purpose you assign to the software. If it is qualified as a medical device, Annex VIII point 6.3 would govern its class, but the passages do not say which class applies to display-only software [3].

sources.title: Definitions
sources.quote:
‘medical device’ means any instrument, apparatus, appliance, software, implant, reagent, material or other article intended by the manufacturer to be used, alone or in combination, for human beings for one or more of the following specific medical purposes:
  — diagnosis, prevention, monitoring, prediction, prognosis, treatment or alleviation of disease,
  — diagnosis, monitoring, treatment, alleviation of, or compensation for, an injury or disability,
  — investigation, replacement or modification of the anatomy or of a physiological or pathological process or state,
  — providing information by means of in vitro examination of specimens derived from the human body, including organ, blood and tissue donations,
  and which does not achieve its principal intended action by pharmacological, immunological or metabolic means, in or on the human body, but which may be assisted in its function by such means.
  The following products shall also be deemed to be medical devices:
  — devices for the control or support of conception;
  — products specifically intended for the cleaning, disinfection or sterilisation of devices as referred to in Article 1(4) and of those referred to in the first paragraph of this point.

question.de: Welche Pflichten habe ich, wenn mein Produkt ein KI-Modell zur Diagnoseunterstützung enthält?
question.en: What obligations do I have if my product contains an AI model for diagnostic support?

de.text: Die Quellen beschreiben die Pflichten eines Anbieters von Hochrisiko-KI-Systemen, darunter Erfüllung der Anforderungen aus Abschnitt 2, ein Qualitätsmanagementsystem, Konformitätsbewertung, EU-Konformitätserklärung und CE-Kennzeichnung [1]. Andere Akteure wie Händler, Importeur, Betreiber oder Dritte werden zum Anbieter mit diesen Pflichten, wenn sie ihren Namen oder ihre Marke auf ein bereits in Verkehr gebrachtes Hochrisiko-KI-System setzen, es wesentlich verändern oder die Zweckbestimmung eines KI-Systems so ändern, dass es zum Hochrisiko-KI-System wird [2][3]. Die Quellen enthalten jedoch keine Einstufungskriterien, sodass nicht geklärt ist, ob ein KI-Modell zur Diagnoseunterstützung ein Hochrisiko-KI-System ist. Sie regeln auch nicht die Pflichten nach der MDR; Recital 84 nennt nur, dass Art. 16(2) MDR für Änderungen an Medizinprodukten weiterhin gilt [3]. Welche Pflichten für Ihr Produkt gelten, hängt daher von Ihrer Rolle und einer Einstufung ab, die die Quellen nicht enthalten.

sources.title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
Responsibilities along the AI value chain
Recital 84
sources.quote: To ensure legal certainty, it is necessary to clarify that, under certain specific conditions, any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party should be considered to be a provider of a high-risk AI system and therefore assume all the relevant obligations. This would be the case if that party puts its name or trademark on a high-risk AI system already placed on the market or put into service, without prejudice to contractual arrangements stipulating that the obligations are allocated otherwise. This would also be the case if that party makes a substantial modification to a high-risk AI system that has already been placed on the market or has already been put into service in a way that it remains a high-risk AI system in accordance with this Regulation, or if it modifies the intended purpose of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which has not been classified as high-risk and has already been placed on the market or put into service, in a way that the AI system becomes a high-risk AI system in accordance with this Regulation. Those provisions should apply without prejudice to more specific provisions established in certain Union harmonisation legislation based on the New Legislative Framework, together with which this Regulation should apply. For example, Article 16(2) of Regulation (EU) 2017/745, establishing that certain changes should not be considered to be modifications of a device that could affect its compliance with the applicable requirements, should continue to apply to high-risk AI systems that are medical devices within the meaning of that Regulation.

de.search_query: obligations of a provider of a high-risk AI system used as medical device diagnostic support, AI Act Article 6 and Article 43 conformity assessment, MDR 2017/745 medical device software requirements

en.text: The passages do not say whether a diagnostic support AI model is high-risk, and they do not establish your role. If your product manufacturer places the AI system on the market under its name or trademark together with the product, or puts it into service under that name after the product is placed on the market, and the AI is a safety component of an Annex I Section A product, you are considered its provider and must meet the Article 16 provider obligations [1][2]. Those obligations include a quality management system, technical documentation, a conformity assessment before placing on the market, an EU declaration of conformity, CE marking and registration [2]. If you are a distributor, importer, deployer or other third party, you become a provider only in the circumstances in Article 25(1), such as putting your name or trademark on a high-risk system already on the market, or making a substantial modification that keeps it high-risk [3]. Recital 84 adds that Article 16(2) of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) continues to apply to high-risk AI systems that are medical devices [4]. The passages do not cover the Article 6 classification criteria or Annex I, so they cannot confirm whether your diagnostic model is high-risk or how the MDR applies to it.

question.de: Darf ich Gesundheitsdaten für das Training eines Modells verwenden?
question.en: May I use health data to train a model?

de.text: Gesundheitsdaten sind besondere Kategorien personenbezogener Daten, deren Verarbeitung grundsätzlich verboten ist [1]. Eine Verarbeitung ist nur zulässig, wenn eine Ausnahme nach Art. 9 Abs. 2 greift, etwa für wissenschaftliche Forschung auf Grundlage von Unions- oder mitgliedstaatlichem Recht mit geeigneten Schutzmaßnahmen [2]. Wissenschaftliche Forschung ist weit auszulegen und kann laut Erwägungsgrund 159 auch technologische Entwicklung und Demonstration umfassen [3]. Die Passagen sagen jedoch nicht ausdrücklich, ob das Training eines Modells unter diese Ausnahme fällt. Eine ausdrückliche Sonderregel findet sich in Art. 10 Abs. 5 des AI Act: Besondere Kategorien personenbezogener Daten dürfen dort nur ausnahmsweise und streng notwendig zur Erkennung und Korrektur von Verzerrungen (Bias) bei Hochrisiko-KI-Systemen verarbeitet werden, und nur bei Erfüllung aller dort genannten Bedingungen, unter anderem dem Fehlen einer wirksamen Alternative mit anderen oder synthetischen bzw. anonymisierten Daten sowie der Löschung nach Abschluss der Bias-Korrektur [4]. Zudem dürfen Mitgliedstaaten weitere Bedingungen oder Einschränkungen für die Verarbeitung von Gesundheitsdaten vorsehen [5][6]. Ob Ihr konkretes Vorhaben zulässig ist, lässt sich anhand der Passagen nicht abschließend beurteilen.

sources.title: Processing of special categories of personal data
sources.quote: Processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership, and the processing of genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited.

sources.title: Processing of special categories of personal data
Recital 159
sources.quote: Where personal data are processed for scientific research purposes, this Regulation should also apply to that processing. For the purposes of this Regulation, the processing of personal data for scientific research purposes should be interpreted in a broad manner including for example technological development and demonstration, fundamental research, applied research and privately funded research. In addition, it should take into account the Union's objective under Article 179(1) TFEU of achieving a European Research Area. Scientific research purposes should also include studies conducted in the public interest in the area of public health. To meet the specificities of processing personal data for scientific research purposes, specific conditions should apply in particular as regards the publication or otherwise disclosure of personal data in the context of scientific research purposes. If the result of scientific research in particular in the health context gives reason for further measures in the interest of the data subject, the general rules of this Regulation should apply in view of those measures.

sources.title: Data and data governance
Processing of special categories of personal data
sources.quote: Member States may maintain or introduce further conditions, including limitations, with regard to the processing of genetic data, biometric data or data concerning health.

sources.title: Recital 53
sources.quote: Special categories of personal data which merit higher protection should be processed for health-related purposes only where necessary to achieve those purposes for the benefit of natural persons and society as a whole, in particular in the context of the management of health or social care services and systems, including processing by the management and central national health authorities of such data for the purpose of quality control, management information and the general national and local supervision of the health or social care system, and ensuring continuity of health or social care and cross-border healthcare or health security, monitoring and alert purposes, or for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes, based on Union or Member State law which has to meet an objective of public interest, as well as for studies conducted in the public interest in the area of public health. Therefore, this Regulation should provide for harmonised conditions for the processing of special categories of personal data concerning health, in respect of specific needs, in particular where the processing of such data is carried out for certain health-related purposes by persons subject to a legal obligation of professional secrecy. Union or Member State law should provide for specific and suitable measures so as to protect the fundamental rights and the personal data of natural persons. Member States should be allowed to maintain or introduce further conditions, including limitations, with regard to the processing of genetic data, biometric data or data concerning health. However, this should not hamper the free flow of personal data within the Union when those conditions apply to cross-border processing of such data.

en.text: The passages only partly answer this. Health data is a special category of personal data [3][2]. The AI Act allows providers of high-risk AI systems to process special categories of personal data only exceptionally, and only to the extent strictly necessary for bias detection and correction [1]. That exception requires all of the following: the bias cannot be effectively addressed with other data, including synthetic or anonymised data; technical limits on re-use and state-of-the-art security measures such as pseudonymisation; strict access controls; no transmission to other parties; deletion once the bias is corrected or the retention period ends; and records of processing that justify the necessity [1]. Training and data governance duties for high-risk systems are set out in [4][5][6]. The passages do not settle whether health data may be used to train a model for other purposes, and they do not state the GDPR legal basis for such processing. GDPR Recital 53 says health data should be processed for health-related purposes only where necessary for those purposes, and that Union or Member State law should provide specific and suitable measures [3].

sources.title: Data and data governance
sources.quote: High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria referred to in paragraphs 2 to 5 whenever such data sets are used.

sources.title: Data and data governance
Recital 67
sources.quote: High-quality data and access to high-quality data plays a vital role in providing structure and in ensuring the performance of many AI systems, especially when techniques involving the training of models are used, with a view to ensure that the high-risk AI system performs as intended and safely and it does not become a source of discrimination prohibited by Union law. High-quality data sets for training, validation and testing require the implementation of appropriate data governance and management practices. Data sets for training, validation and testing, including the labels, should be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose of the system. In order to facilitate compliance with Union data protection law, such as Regulation (EU) 2016/679, data governance and management practices should include, in the case of personal data, transparency about the original purpose of the data collection. The data sets should also have the appropriate statistical properties, including as regards the persons or groups of persons in relation to whom the high-risk AI system is intended to be used, with specific attention to the mitigation of possible biases in the data sets, that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where data outputs influence inputs for future operations (feedback loops). Biases can for example be inherent in underlying data sets, especially when historical data is being used, or generated when the systems are implemented in real world settings. Results provided by AI systems could be influenced by such inherent biases that are inclined to gradually increase and thereby perpetuate and amplify existing discrimination, in particular for persons belonging to certain vulnerable groups, including racial or ethnic groups.

question.de: In welche Risikoklasse fällt Software, die Entscheidungen für Diagnose oder Therapie unterstützt?
question.en: Which risk class does software that supports diagnostic or therapeutic decisions fall into?

de.text: Software, die Informationen liefert, die zur Entscheidungsfindung für diagnostische oder therapeutische Zwecke verwendet werden, fällt grundsätzlich in Klasse IIa [1]. Sie gehört zu Klasse III, wenn die Entscheidungen Tod oder eine irreversible Verschlechterung des Gesundheitszustands verursachen können, und zu Klasse IIb, wenn sie eine ernsthafte Verschlechterung des Gesundheitszustands oder einen chirurgischen Eingriff verursachen können [1]. Die Passagen legen nicht fest, wie die Auswirkung im Einzelfall zu bestimmen ist.

en.text: Software intended to provide information used to take decisions with diagnosis or therapeutic purposes is classified as class IIa under Rule 11 (Annex VIII, point 6.3) [1]. It is class IIb if those decisions may cause a serious deterioration of a person's state of health or a surgical intervention, and class III if they may cause death or an irreversible deterioration of a person's state of health [1]. Software that drives a device or influences its use falls in the same class as that device, while independent software is classified in its own right [2]. The passages do not state how to determine in a specific case whether a decision's impact reaches these severity thresholds.

question.de: Welche allgemeinen Pflichten haben Hersteller von Medizinprodukten nach der MDR?
question.en: What are the general obligations of manufacturers of medical devices under the MDR?

de.text: Hersteller müssen sicherstellen, dass ihre Produkte bei Inverkehrbringen oder Inbetriebnahme gemäß den Anforderungen der MDR ausgelegt und hergestellt wurden [1]. Sie müssen das Post-Market-Surveillance-System gemäß Art. 83 einrichten und auf aktuellem Stand halten [2]. Zudem müssen sie die UDI-Pflichten nach Art. 27 sowie die Registrierungspflichten nach Art. 29 und 31 erfüllen [3]. Wenn Produkte von einer anderen Person ausgelegt oder hergestellt werden, gehört deren Identität zu den nach Art. 29(4) zu übermittelnden Informationen [4]. Hersteller von Sonderanfertigungen müssen zudem Dokumentation nach Abschnitt 2 des Anhangs XIII erstellen, aktuell halten und den zuständigen Behörden zur Verfügung stellen [5]. Die Passagen legen nicht im Einzelnen fest, welche weiteren Pflichten aus Art. 10 bestehen; Art. 11(4) besagt lediglich, dass bestimmte Pflichten nicht delegiert werden können [6].

sources.title: General obligations of manufacturers
sources.quote: When placing their devices on the market or putting them into service, manufacturers shall ensure that they have been designed and manufactured in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation.

sources.title: General obligations of manufacturers
sources.quote: Manufacturers of devices shall implement and keep up to date the post-market surveillance system in accordance with Article 83.

sources.title: General obligations of manufacturers
sources.quote: Manufacturers shall comply with the obligations relating to the UDI system referred to in Article 27 and with the registration obligations referred to in Articles 29 and 31.

sources.title: General obligations of manufacturers
sources.quote: Where manufacturers have their devices designed or manufactured by another legal or natural person the information on the identity of that person shall be part of the information to be submitted in accordance with Article 29(4).

sources.title: General obligations of manufacturers
sources.quote: Manufacturers of custom-made devices shall draw up, keep up to date and keep available for competent authorities documentation in accordance with Section 2 of Annex XIII.

sources.quote: The mandate referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article shall not delegate the manufacturer's obligations laid down in Article 10(1), (2), (3), (4), (6), (7), (9), (10), (11) and (12).

en.text: Manufacturers must draw up and keep up to date technical documentation for non-custom-made devices, which must allow conformity assessment and include the elements of Annexes II and III [1]. They must establish, document, implement, maintain and continually improve a quality management system proportionate to risk class and device type, covering aspects such as regulatory compliance strategy, risk management under Annex I Section 3, and clinical evaluation under Article 61 and Annex XIV [2][3]. They must also establish, document, implement and maintain a risk management system per Annex I Section 3 [4], keep technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity available for at least 10 years (15 years for implantable devices) after the last device is placed on the market [5], and implement and keep up to date a post-market surveillance system under Article 83 [6]. The passages do not provide a complete list of all manufacturer obligations under the MDR.
